detections.evidence_quote: there is likely a metabolic problem, an underpowering mitochondrial dysfunction
detections.summary: Speaker presents mitochondrial/metabolic dysfunction as the root cause underlying most chronic diseases, driven by modern lifestyle and environmental changes.

detections.evidence_quote: that is research that came out a couple years ago
detections.summary: An unnamed study is cited as the source of the 93.2% metabolic-dysfunction statistic.

detections.evidence_quote: anything that doesn't have enough power is going to become dysfunctional, like a sputtering car or a dysfunctional factory
detections.summary: Cell/mitochondria mechanism vocabulary (underpowered cells, factories) is used to explain the dysfunction narrative.

detections.evidence_quote: the eighty thousand plus synthetic chemicals that are now created in factories that live in our food, water, air, personal care products
detections.summary: Synthetic chemicals and environmental exposures are invoked in general terms as harming mitochondria.

detections.evidence_quote: we have to fix the metabolic dysfunction, and we can greatly transform the health
detections.summary: The chronic disease epidemic is framed as predictable and fixable by addressing one underlying root cause (metabolic dysfunction).

verification_candidates.claim_text: At least 93.2% of American adults have at least one biomarker of metabolic dysfunction.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: at least 93.2% of American adults have at least one biomarker of metabolic dysfunction
verification_candidates.rationale: This prevalence statistic is attributed to research and is a specific, checkable figure worth verifying against the source study.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Mitochondrial/metabolic dysfunction in brain cells underlies a wide range of conditions, including migraines, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, Alzheimer's dementia, neurodevelopmental disorders, depression, and anxiety.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: It could look like migraines, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, Alzheimer's dementia, neurodevelopmental disorders, depression, or anxiety.
verification_candidates.rationale: This sweeping causal claim linking mitochondrial dysfunction to many unrelated diseases needs evidence checking given its scope.

verification_candidates.claim_text: More than fifty percent of the U.S. population used to work in agriculture, on their feet all day, versus less than one percent today.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: It used to be that over fifty percent of the country was involved in agriculture, on their feet all day.
verification_candidates.rationale: This historical occupational statistic, used to support the sedentary-lifestyle causal narrative, is checkable against labor data.
